key_insight: BeatGraph represents infant ECG by heartbeat, not fixed patches, so the model preserves cardiac structure and adapts to changing heart rates.
engineering_relevance: This heartbeat-level graph design improves self-supervised ECG representations for real-world infant monitoring and transfers well across pediatric and adult benchmarks.
method: Encodes each heartbeat with a shared beat encoder using waveform and inter-beat interval information.
Uses a Transformer with positional encoding to order beats within a 30-second window.
Applies residual graph attention and attention pooling, then pretrains by predicting masked-beat embeddings.
evidence_signal: Pretraining and fine-tuning on 3,408 hours of single-channel ECG from 143 infants yielded macro-F1 gains of 0.076 to 0.158 across infant tasks, 0.892 AUROC on ZZU-pECG, and linear-evaluation performance matching a strong adult ECG model on PTB-XL.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable heartbeat segmentation and may be sensitive to noisy home-recorded ECG or missed beats.
paper_title: BeatGraph: Self-Supervised Heartbeat Graphs for Infant ECG Representations from the Home Environment
